edges.section: ['§2.6 Building.households (clamped into [1, capacity] for a residential building)', '§2.6 capacity (a slot without hous
edges.edge: A residential building is clamped into [1, capacity] and "every residential building houses ... at least one household", while capacity is 0 for a building S11 builds for a slot without houses (BuildingSlot.unhoused reads as such) and floor(Σ A(s)·(den−num)/(2·den·minRoomCm2)) can be 0 for a very small residential shell; the clamp interval [1, 0] and the at-least-one guarantee then conflict, and the outcome is not defined.
Basement access age term with one growth stage (K = 1): 'age ∈ [0,1] the plot's growth-stage rank (1 for the first stage, 0 for the last)' is undefined when first = last.

Dug connector: target beyond digReachM but reachable by a route ≤ 2 × digReachM — step (2) limits targets to digReachM, step (3) refuses routes longer than 2 × digReachM; the case where no target is within digReachM goes to step (4). Consistent, but the refusal test for a target within digReachM whose route exceeds 2 × digReachM has no test named.
S12c on pseudo-districts (hinterland, sky, underground, undercity) — see CF-PIPE-06.
Catacomb source age with a staged HistoryHint: 'replaced by the staged HistoryHint.ageYears' — whether every source takes the settlement's age or its stage-scaled age is not stated.
Sewer and undercity light 'fuel by the settlement's circumstances' — which circumstance row selects which fuel rows is not stated.
Island 'count' as a setAttr/lock target — the record that holds the count (the slots) is not named.
Ring spacing factor 1 + f is stated as '[1, 2)' but the folded bell reaches 1 when every uniform is 0, so 2 is reachable.
Underground institution depth 8–15 m is stated as a value while the granularity 'institution / assigned' row gives depth 'by requirement' — the depthScale rule cannot produce it.

A region group may name 'any set of nodes whose districts are disjoint' - not necessarily contiguous - and its spine is 'from the union of the members' faces by §9.3's area rule', which is defined for one face (simplify, hole-aware skeleton, spine); the outcome for a union of several components (one spine on the largest, one per component, a leader) is undefined and untested.

The knowledge filter's list of always-`public` rows (ways, districts, quarters, water bodies, woods, gates, the title, annotations) omits the kinds `region`, `landmark`, `place` and `address`; landmark, place and address take their target's record, but a region row's knownTo has no stated source.

The greedy's default priority order (region > quarter / district > water > landmark > place > gate > way > address) omits the LabelEntity kinds `wood` and `annotation`, so their default priority - and hence their place in the strict order - is unstated.

The island rows draw `waning` / `settled` at 'alpha x 0.8 / alpha x 0.6 with the ghost share raised (§8.4)'; §8.4 defines only ghostAlpha (default 0.35) - whether 'raised' is the effect of the alpha factor or a separate raise, and by how much, is undefined.

Undefined inputs of the storey-height rule: E(w) = deckLevel(w) - heights.baseCm <= 0 or below one riser per storey (a degenerate or edited wing), and G + (n - 1) x U = 0 in the ratio; and for s < 0 'the baseCm of the ground wing above' when the basement ring spans ground wings of different baseCm (which wing's datum sets each basement storey) - no defined outcome, fallback or test (principle (11)).

L5's dug pieces for a subterranean dossier institution are 'held while that institution is live' (delete refused dossier-owned); what becomes of them when the dossier removes or closes the institution (an epoch's dossier phase or an absorb) is not stated - kept as closed dug elements (the underground is never torn down), re-derived, or removed with the institution - nor tested (principle (11): a dossier removing what an edit or rule pinned).

The reading counts links of kind secret and accesses in state locked as joins to the surface for every viewer, so a cluster reached only through a secret link is 'accessible' (dwellings may settle) while its knownTo hides the way; the outcome for dwellers vs viewers is defined, but the interplay with g item 113 (e)'s 'access counts only through OPEN links' is undefined (see the missing finding).

A locked island (or locked state path) whose institution the dossier removes: (1b) re-reasons the island (rewrites reason and institution by conversion), while 'A locked island, or a locked state, areaHa or altitudeCm path, is held by these steps (§7.2)'. The outcome of a dossier removal against a lock — held as an institution island with no institution, or re-reasoned despite the lock — is undefined and untested (principle (11)'s 'a dossier removing what an edit pinned').

edges.section: V5 §3.16 (2)-(4) combined with another island's access
edges.edge: A landfall whose footprint covers another island's ground landing plot or access foot is not defined: the covered set includes every L3 plot (so the landing house is demolished and the use vacated) but nothing states what happens to the other island's SkyAccess (closed, unserved, re-landed, or its island left unreachable) until a re-derivation re-sites it.

edges.section: V5 §4.2 placeSkyAccess vs §2.3b '≤ 9 entries' and §6 budget
edges.edge: No cap limits hand-placed accesses per island (placeSkyAccess checks kind, magic and run only; accessCount.max binds generated accesses), yet §2.3b and §6 bound skyAccessObstacles at '≤ 9 entries per document' and price the solver on that bound; the maximum-access edge is undefined.

The sky.clearance step's lock case — a locked island or altitudeCm path keeps elevationCm, the floor may fail, the conflict 'clearance held by your lock' is listed and the island is exempt from the clearance invariant — has no test (T-V5-31 (b) and T-V5-10 test only unlocked islands).

Degenerate advance inputs have no defined outcome: a spanYears below half a week rounds spanYears × 52 to 0, so W_n = W0 and f_i = (W_i − W0) ÷ (W_n − W0) is 0 ÷ 0; cadenceWeeks ≤ 0 (the field is a free number) makes n = ⌈spanYears × 52 ÷ cadenceWeeks⌉ undefined; a points trajectory with unsorted or duplicate weeks, or a negative target or perYear ≤ −1, is not addressed (the clamp covers only the result); no test (T-V6-23) exercises them.

An advance group undoes 'by restoring the checkpoint taken before the group's first epoch … in an unshared document'; the outcome is undefined (and untested) when the document was saved and reloaded after the group (checkpoints and the history store are memory, not saved) and when the document is shared (the truncation is stated only for an unshared one) — principle (11)'s 'an epoch undone after a save'.

J-VI.4 (f) (docs/volumes/_integrate.md) bends a raised course that would cut a sky access's column or rope line, where skyAccessObstacles offers no re-route, to end at the last ground vertex before it ('this would cut {island}'s hoist; it ends here'). V09 — which carries every bend row (T-V9-15 fails CI on a code with no row) and words J-VI.4 (d), (e), (g), (h) — has no catalogue row, no rule text in §4.20.2 and no clause in T-V9-52 for case (f): a combination edge (a raised way under an island's access) without a defined wording or test on the canvas.

edges.section: V10 §4.2 (3) creation acceptance and V09 §4.11 creation preview vs V09 §3.2 (3) the empty state
edges.edge: V10 says that when a creation proposal replaces the untouched empty-state town 'the old handle closes — nothing is lost, the old town being its seed and still in the recent documents (R15)', and V09 §4.11 says 'the old one stays in Recent towns'; but V09 §3.2 (3) writes nothing to the local store while the log holds only its creation prefix (the LocalDocRecord is created on the first committed event), and the Recent grid (§5.13) lists stored towns. The edge 'accept an assistant's new town while the untouched empty-state town is open' has two outcomes in the set: the old town is recoverable fro

edges.section: V11 §3.24.5 'The rule' and 'The pre-decided failure for a cart class'
edges.edge: A crossing is a ramp (step over run <= rampMaxGrade, or a switchback within minTerraceDepthM), else a stair when the class has one; a cart class takes a ramp 'up to 1.5 x rampMaxGrade' (W_STEEP_RAMP), 'never a stair and never a gap'. The case where a cart class's crossing needs more than 1.5 x rampMaxGrade and no switchback fits (e.g. a 4 m step, stepMaxCm 400, on a through way at 0.08 with a short run) has no stated outcome (reroute, lower the step, lengthen the ramp past the terrace, or refuse). PLAUSIBLE: reasoning from the text.

Satisfaction clamp(2 - n / target, 0, 1) and the households radius sqrt(per x a_res / pi) are undefined for target = 0 or per = 0 (and a_res = 0 in a district with no residential plots); no range for per/target is stated in the schema comment. PLAUSIBLE.
